newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Modern plans 180 MW power plant.
newsitem.headline: India's Modern plans 180 MW power plant.

text.p: Modern Threads is studying the feasibility of building a naphtha-fired power plant in India's western state of Gujarat, its chairman said on Monday.
"We have agreement (in principle) of the Gujarat government," H.S. Ranka, chairman of the Modern Group, told reporters.

Modern Threads is implementing a 16.6 billion rupee integrated project to manufacture 170,000 tonnes of paraxylene and 250,000 tonnes of polyester input purified terephthalic acid (PTA) a year, using raw naphtha as raw material.
Modern would use 360,400 tonnes of naphtha a year, he said.

Ranka said Modern's project would extract a "special cut" of naphtha for making paraxylene. The balance is normally returned to naphtha suppliers but Modern was studying the possibility of building a power plant using this naphtha as a fuel, he said.
